verdicts.evidence: Ledger (rsc vault logins, 2026-10-30T20:15Z..10-31T18:38Z): 31 logins (30 boot + 1 relogin); boot outcomes 9 restored / 11 locked / 9 challenge / 1 failed, so the count and wall rate are CONFIRMED. rs-fleet-agent logs: desired.count changed 13 times (8->10->9->10->6->8->9->6->4->6->8->7->8->9), 72 exit-75 replaces, 56 of them on homelab-8. Against the mechanism: homelab-8 had 56 exit-75 replaces but only 3 ledger logins, so a fenced or slotless restart exits before any login. The 31 logins were on 29 distinct devices, no device that ended 'locked' logged in again in the window, and the only same-device repeat after a wall was one challenge->challenge 2 h apart. plan.ts:35-36 SOFT_LIMIT/SOFT_BACKOFF_MS only stretches the delay to 10 min and never parks, as claimed. Details: docs/review-2026-10-31/repro/B3-verify/B3-01-evidence.md
verdicts.reason: Two parts are reproduced: the login volume and the 68% wall rate, and that the logins cluster at slot-count changes, which apps/backend/src/fleet/hosts.ts:239 workerCount computes from free and held slots, not a person. The P1 core is not supported: exit-75 restart loops do not log in, and locked accounts are not logged in again hours later. Repeat logins on one slot are different devices, which means different accounts if the device-to-account binding holds. What is left is the pool burning fresh accounts at boot, as count changes move slots and fence and re-home running workers (10:25 count 10->6, logins 10:27-10:30), plus a soft backoff that never stops. That makes it a P2 drift or ops risk, not a P1 code defect.
